official_sources: Natural England rural land change guidance
Natural Environment and Rural Communities Act 2006
official_measurement_examples: Agricultural EIA protects uncultivated semi-natural and rural land from specified changes
screening decision is required before applicable work starts
screening opinion is not consent where significant effects require further assessment
cultivated land can still qualify as semi-natural in some cases
restructuring rural land is a distinct project type
agricultural EIA consent is distinct from planning permission
EIA status does not establish ownership or final development yield
core_rules: planning permission is not agricultural EIA consent
uncultivated and semi-natural tests remain distinct
cultivation history does not automatically remove semi-natural status
restructuring is a distinct project type
work must not start before required decision
absence from register is not proof no duty applies
enforcement status is distinct from consent status
agricultural EIA does not establish ownership
agricultural EIA does not establish access rights
agricultural EIA does not calculate yield
no parcel agricultural-EIA clearance or Future Growth score may be promoted while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official Natural England, Defra, GOV.UK and legislation sources checked 2026-07-26. 1 July 2026 public-register currentity retained; no parcel promotion.
